explanation: Staling is mostly starch molecules recrystallizing, not bread drying out, and that happens fastest at fridge temperatures. Freezing stops it, and warming stale bread briefly reverses it.

claims.text: Bread stales faster at refrigerator temperatures than at room temperature.
Bread staling is caused mainly by starch retrogradation, the recrystallization of starch, rather than by drying out.
Starch retrogradation in bread is fastest at temperatures just above freezing, such as those in a fridge.
Briefly reheating stale bread reverses much of the staling.
